items.headline: Ratings (buy/hold/sell): 26/1/0 → 26/2/0 — Nasdaq.com / Zacks
FY27 consensus EPS: $174.19 → $174.66 (+0.3%) — Nasdaq.com / Zacks
FY28 consensus EPS: $212.33 → $216.17 (+1.8%) — Nasdaq.com / Zacks
Mean price target: $1,624.42 → $1,573.52 (-3.1%) — Nasdaq.com / Zacks
Low price target: $1,200.00 → $775.00 (-35.4%) — Nasdaq.com / Zacks

HBM customers: Google is pursuing direct purchases of HBM for its in-house TPUs instead of going through Broadcom, working with MediaTek on its next-generation TPU (DigiTimes report). Counterpoint estimates Broadcom's model adds a 15–20% intermediary margin to HBM costs and sees AI-ASIC HBM bit demand rising 35-fold from 2024 to 2028 (third-party est.); Korean suppliers see more direct customer access but also more buyer pricing power (The Asia Business Daily (citing DigiTimes, Counterpoint), 2026-11-28)
MU closed $646.95 on 2026-11-27, +8.8% vs $594.51 on 2026-11-20 (Nasdaq.com official closes)

MU +7.60% to $646.95 on 27 Nov (half-day session, 1:00 pm ET close; range $607.27–$654.33, ~26.9M shares) from $601.25 on 25 Nov, as investors bought beaten-down AI chip names after Thanksgiving. SOX +4.7%, Nasdaq +2.31%, S&P 500 +1.60%; SanDisk +15.96%, Seagate +7.90%, Western Digital +7.22%, Nvidia +0.8%. MU ended after-hours at $645.66 (−0.20%, 4:59 pm ET). MU is still ~47% below its 25 Jun closing high of $1,213.56 (Reuters (via Investing.com); Nasdaq.com, 2026-11-27)

Pricing outlook (TrendForce, third-party est., 27 Nov): buyers and suppliers have been reworking 2027–28 plans since early 4Q26, slightly slowing DRAM buying. Base case: conventional DRAM contract price gains narrow through 2027, level off in 2H27 and decline across all products from 1Q28 as bit supply keeps growing strongly. Bear case (server OEM cuts, supply-chain destocking, neocloud consolidation, tighter BIS controls): declines start in 4Q27 and widen in 2028. Risks cited: post-midterm US data-centre policy, power limits, possible Nvidia cut-back in neocloud financing and BIS chip-access rules. No HBM figures given (TrendForce, 2026-11-27)

Pricing risk (Bank of Korea, third-party est.): a BoK study released 26 Nov modelled 2028 HBM and conventional DRAM prices 51% below its baseline if slower AI investment, tighter financing and faster Chinese supply growth hit together. The baseline (Gartner) already has prices −23% y/y in 2028. Tighter financing was the largest single shock (−30% vs baseline in 2028; Chinese supply −20%, investment delays −16%). Scenario, not the central forecast; NAND not covered (AI Industry Today summary) (DIGITIMES (Bank of Korea study, 26 Nov), 2026-11-27)

Competitors (27 Nov close, Seoul): KOSPI +4.34% to 4,915.68 on hopes the ₩10T market stabilisation fund will be expanded; foreigners net bought ₩1.13T, the most since 7 Sep. Samsung Electronics +4.55% to ₩179,100; SK hynix +5.41% to ₩1.11M on its ex-dividend day, after both opened lower (Yonhap; Korea Times, 2026-11-27)

Largest HBM customer / export policy: Singapore Deputy PM Gan Kim Yong said on 27 Nov that Singapore has not confirmed reports that Nvidia halted server shipments to Southeast Asia. Singapore is asking companies about the impact and reviewing its rules and monitoring so the country does not become a conduit for illegal chip trade (CNA, 2026-11-27)

Taiwan labour: after four hours at the 26 Nov mediation, Micron agreed to give the Taoyuan union the reward-plan briefing materials shown to employees since 22 Oct, under confidentiality. The union will submit its own proposal on 2 Dec, and the third mediation is set for the morning of 4 Dec (Taoyuan labour bureau) (ETtoday (Taoyuan city labour bureau), 2026-11-27)

Spot pricing (TrendForce / DRAMeXchange, third-party, 27 Nov GMT+8): DDR5 16Gb $60.333 (−0.71%), DDR4 16Gb $76.625 (−1.13%), DDR4 8Gb $42.714 (−0.95%). Week on week (vs 20 Nov): DDR5 −0.55%, DDR4 16Gb −2.54%, DDR4 8Gb −2.37%. NAND wafer spot not updated since 16 Nov (TrendForce / DRAMeXchange, 2026-11-27)

Competitors (27 Nov, Asia): in Korean pre-market trading (Nextrade, 08:06 KST) Samsung Electronics was +0.29% at ₩171,800 and SK hynix −0.76% at ₩1.045M, with US markets shut for Thanksgiving. On 26 Nov the KOSPI closed +0.29% at 4,711.21 (Samsung +0.35% to ₩171,300, SK hynix +2.23% to ₩1.053M) after giving back an early 2.6% gain as the Bank of Korea raised its policy rate to 3.25% and Nvidia's Southeast Asia shipment halt was reported (Yonhap) (Newsis (Nextrade pre-market), 2026-11-27)

No US session on 26 Nov (Thanksgiving); MU's last close is still $601.25 (25 Nov). It ended the 25 Nov after-hours session at ~$615.2 (+2.3%). Fri 27 Nov is a half-day session (1:00 pm ET close). Consensus targets unchanged: S&P Global mean $1,530 (49 analysts, low $361, high $3,000) (StockAnalysis; Public.com; NYSE holiday calendar, 2026-11-26)

Taiwan labour: the second Micron–Taoyuan union mediation, convened ex officio by the Taoyuan city government on 26 Nov, ended without a deal; the union agreed to hand Micron its own proposal on 2 Dec, and a third mediation is set for 4 Dec at 9:00 am Taiwan time (Liberty Times (Taoyuan city labour bureau), 2026-11-26)

Pricing outlook cut (GF Securities, third-party est., 26 Nov): Jeff Pu cut his 2027 DRAM contract price forecast to +6%, +3%, 0% and 0% q/q for 1Q–4Q27 (from +10%, +7%, +5%, +3%), citing trimmed Chinese CSP server orders and soft consumer demand. His first 2028 scenarios put conventional DRAM at $8/GB in the base case (−50% from 2027's ~$16), $4 bear and $12 bull, with HBM −20% base. He still sees DRAM undersupplied (−5%/−5%/−4% sufficiency in 2026–28) and stays constructive on Micron and SK hynix (Wccftech (GF Securities note via Zhitong Finance), 2026-11-26)

Spot pricing (TrendForce / DRAMeXchange, third-party, 26 Nov GMT+8): DDR5 16Gb $60.767 (flat), DDR4 16Gb $77.50 (−0.32%), DDR4 8Gb $43.125 (−0.21%). TrendForce says order visibility is poor, most buyers remain bearish and branded chip prices keep being revised down (TrendForce / DRAMeXchange, 2026-11-26)

Largest HBM customer: Nvidia told server partners including Dell and Supermicro to stop shipping servers with its chips to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia while it assesses compliance with the BIS licence rule in force since 19 Nov; it is unclear whether the halt is temporary (FT via Reuters). Fitch said the curbs will slow and narrow Asia-Pacific data-centre investment, with neocloud operators under the most pressure (Reuters (citing FT); Reuters (Fitch), 2026-11-26)

Competitors (NAND): Kioxia rose as much as 14.5% to ¥7,895 in Tokyo on 26 Nov after a proof of concept with Nvidia extended effective GPU memory with SSDs: 144 Kioxia XD8 drives (~1.1 PB raw, ~80x the rack's 13.4 TB of HBM) in a GB200 NVL72 rack, said to support up to 2 trillion vectors; the companies are still evaluating performance. In US overnight trading SanDisk was ~+4% and MU ~+2% (Stocktwits) (Investing.com; Stocktwits, 2026-11-26)

China competitors: Samsung and SK hynix have agreed to adopt parts of YMTC's Xtacking 3D NAND stacking technology through patent cross-licensing (Nikkei Asia). The draft ISSCC Feb 2027 program lists CXMT papers on next-generation DDR5 and an LPDDR6 interface and a Huawei next-generation HBM paper (data-pin density reportedly twice current mass-production parts); CXMT said earlier in November it had validated engineering samples of a 4F² sixth-generation DRAM platform (Financial News (citing Yicai, Nikkei Asia), 2026-11-26)

Competitors (Asia): on 25 Nov the KOSPI fell 6.16% as Samsung Electronics closed −9.87% at ₩170,700 (market cap below ₩1,000T) and SK hynix −11.05% at ₩1.03M. In 26 Nov pre-market trading Samsung was +1.29% (₩173,000) and SK hynix +2.43% (₩1.05M) after US indices pared losses (MoneyToday; Aju Press, 2026-11-26)

Target cut: UBS's Timothy Arcuri lowered his Micron price target to $1,100 from $1,625 and kept a Buy rating, partly unwinding his May call that tripled the target on long-term supply agreements. TipRanks' 3-month average target is now $1,573.52 (30 analysts, 'Strong Buy') (Benzinga; StockAnalysis (TipRanks data), 2026-11-25)

MU fell 4.53% on 25 Nov to close at $601.25 (from $629.79; opened $574.96, range $548.13–$604.95, ~52M shares), having been down ~13% intraday before paring losses; it is down 15% from the 23 Nov close. Nvidia −3.91% (−9% intraday) as the Huang-return rally faded; PHLX Semiconductor index −0.65% (−7.96% intraday), Nasdaq Composite −0.62%, S&P 500 −0.25%, Dow +0.33%; the PCE price index rose 3.8% y/y (Aju Press). US markets are closed on 26 Nov (Thanksgiving) (Nasdaq.com; CNBC; Aju Press, 2026-11-25)

Hyperscaler capex (Goldman Sachs, third-party est., 25 Nov): sees hyperscaler capex at ~$1.1T in 2027 and $1.2–1.3T in 2028, with memory ~44% of capex in 2027 falling to ~40% in 2028 as memory prices fall. If 2028 capex is flat, −10% or −20% vs 2027, memory spending would be $55B, $99B or $144B lower. Still constructive on 2027; cautious on 2028 (AI capex durability, weak phone/PC demand, more Chinese supply) (ETEnterpriseAI (ANI, Goldman Sachs note), 2026-11-25)

Competitors (25 Nov, Asia): Samsung Electronics (−4.4%, ₩181,000) and SK hynix (−4.8%, ₩1.10M) fell in Korean pre-market trading after the US chip slide, having closed up 6.70% and 6.73% on 24 Nov; KOSPI night futures −4.56% (Newsis (via Financial News); Aju Press, 2026-11-25)

Pricing outlook cut (TrendForce, third-party est., 25 Nov): Chinese CSPs cut 2027 memory orders, so TrendForce lowered its 2027 DRAM revenue forecast to $1.15T (+69% y/y) and NAND to $419.3B (+29%). Some Chinese CSPs began trimming 2027 server DRAM bit demand outside LTAs in early 4Q26, but North American CSPs absorbed the supply; DRAM stays tight through 2027 with quarterly contract increases narrowing and possibly levelling off in 2H27. NAND enters a downward pricing cycle as supply expands (1Q27 NAND contract 0% to −5%, per its 19 Nov release) (TrendForce (press release); Wall Street Observer, 2026-11-25)

Tariff policy: USTR found 'structural excess capacity' practices of 14 economies actionable under Section 301 and proposed tariffs on nearly all their goods: up to 15% for Japan, Korea and Taiwan (net of MFN), up to 20% for Singapore and China, 35% for Vietnam. Not yet in effect: comments due 5 Jan 2027, hearings from 25 Jan 2027. For 13 of the 14 (not China), goods already under Section 232 tariffs, including semiconductors, would be exempt (Baker McKenzie) (USTR; Baker McKenzie, 2026-11-25)

Spot pricing (TrendForce / DRAMeXchange, third-party, 25 Nov GMT+8): DDR5 16Gb $60.767 (−0.11%), DDR4 16Gb $77.75 (−0.64%), DDR4 8Gb $43.214 (−0.25%). TrendForce's 25 Nov DRAM bulletin says spot buying is weak as buyers cut inventory first, and that Nanya and Winbond are filling the consumer DRAM gap while major suppliers focus on server products (TrendForce / DRAMeXchange, 2026-11-25)

Largest HBM customer: reinstated Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang faces a closed-door House interview (Foreign Affairs, Intelligence and China committees) on 1 Dec and public testimony at the Senate Banking Committee on export controls on 3 Dec, covering advanced-chip flows to China and the circumstances of his return (Lianhe Zaobao (agencies), 2026-11-25)
SEC filing: ARS (filed 2026-11-24)
SEC filing: DEFA14A (filed 2026-11-24)
SEC filing: DEF 14A (filed 2026-11-24)

Proxy filed (SEC, 24 Nov): Micron's FY2026 annual meeting is set for 14 Jan 2027 (virtual, record date 18 Nov). Proposals: elect 8 directors (Linnie Haynesworth retiring), say-on-pay, add 15M shares to the ESPP and 20M shares to the 2025 Equity Incentive Plan (38.7M shares left as of 30 Oct), ratify PwC; the Board opposes two shareholder proposals (10% special-meeting right; critical-minerals just-transition report). CEO Sanjay Mehrotra's FY2026 summary compensation: $39.7M (FY2025: $30.9M) (SEC EDGAR (Micron DEF 14A, DEFA14A, ARS), 2026-11-24)

Downgrade: BNP Paribas Exane's Karl Ackerman cut Micron to Neutral from Outperform and its target to $775 from $1,700 (new Street low on TipRanks), warning that oversupply risk is mounting: he sees DRAM/NAND supply and demand approaching parity from mid-2027 (previously mid-2028), with ASP declines, citing risks to 2028 hyperscaler capacity plans, less HBM in Nvidia's Vera Rubin Ultra, falling PC/phone units and new wafer capacity. BNP's CY2028 EPS is 45% below consensus, with a trough of $86 in CY2029 (third-party est.) (Investing.com; MarketWatch; TipRanks, 2026-11-24)

MU fell 11.01% on 24 Nov to close at $629.79 (official Nasdaq close; first reported as $627.74, −11.30%) (from $707.70; ~39M shares), giving back most of Monday's 19% jump after the BNP downgrade, as the AI-chip sell-off resumed: Nvidia −5.9%, SK hynix ADR −9.9%, AMD −8.9%, SanDisk ~−14%, PHLX Semiconductor index −7.88%, Nasdaq −1.48%, S&P 500 −0.50% (Dow +0.85%); Anthropic (ANT) slipped below its $83 IPO price (Nasdaq.com historical; MarketWatch; Benzinga, 2026-11-24)

Spot pricing (TrendForce / DRAMeXchange, third-party, 24 Nov GMT+8): DDR5 16Gb $60.833 (+0.22%), DDR4 16Gb $78.25 (−0.32%), DDR4 8Gb $43.321 (−0.49%). Bank of America (via TechRadar, 24 Nov) puts 512Gb NAND wafer spot at $14.30 (−12% w/w, −32% q/q), expects PC/phone NAND contract −5–10% in 1Q27, and keeps DRAM contract forecasts of +8% in 4Q26 and +5% in 1Q27 (estimates) (TrendForce / DRAMeXchange; TechRadar (Bank of America est.), 2026-11-24)

Tariff policy: POLITICO reports USTR Jamieson Greer was set to propose new Section 301 tariff hikes on the EU, China, Mexico, Japan and 12 other partners on 24 Nov over excess manufacturing capacity; separately, President Trump said in a 23 Nov CNBC interview he expects chip imports to face 200% tariffs in two years (no implementing action published; the current Section 232 rule is 25% on certain advanced computing chips with US data-centre and other exemptions) (POLITICO; Newsmerica (CNBC interview), 2026-11-24)

Customer read-through: Hewlett Packard Enterprise said on its Q4 FY26 call that memory, NAND and other critical components will stay supply-constrained through at least 2H 2028; component price increases were double-digit in FY26 and are expected to ease in 2027, and HPE will keep passing costs to customers while guiding lower Cloud & AI operating margins (HPE (Q4 FY26 earnings call, via The Motley Fool); The Asia Business Daily, 2026-11-24)

HBM capacity (third-party est.): Korean industry sources say Micron is pulling forward HBM equipment orders, mainly Hanmi TC bonders, for Singapore and Taiwan; its ~$7B Singapore HBM packaging plant (first tool-in 19 Nov) targets initial output in early 2027. Estimates put Micron's HBM wafer input at ~100k wafers/month by end-2026 (about double a year earlier, ~half of Samsung's or SK hynix's); Counterpoint puts Q2 2026 HBM share at SK hynix 50%, Samsung 33%, Micron 18% (Chosun Biz (industry sources; Counterpoint est.), 2026-11-24)

Competitors (24 Nov, Asia): SK hynix traded ~12% higher (₩1.217M) and Samsung Electronics ~10% higher (₩194,700) in Korean pre-market trading after Huang's return, following a 23 Nov KOSPI close of −3.31% (Samsung −3.06%, SK hynix −2.52%, both at their lowest closes since March–April); KOSPI 200 night futures rose 7.06% (Chosun Biz; Yonhap, 2026-11-24)

Taiwan labour: the Micron Taoyuan union rejected Micron's proposal in its 21–24 Nov member vote: 1,567 of 1,852 voters (84.6%) against, 282 (15.2%) for. The union asked Micron to bring a reasonable proposal to the 26 Nov mediation meeting and opposes the peace-obligation clause; no production disruption reported (Liberty Times (Taiwan), 2026-11-24)

MU jumped 19.04% on 23 Nov to close at $707.70 (from $594.51; range $666.66–$720.69, ~49M shares, ~72% above its 3-month average), ending a seven-session losing streak, after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO and Citi called the memory sell-off overdone; PHLX Semiconductor index +14.03%, Nasdaq Composite +6.51% (best day since April 2025), S&P 500 +4.73%; Nvidia +31.48%, SK hynix ADR +20.00%, Dell +20.46%, Western Digital +13.84%. MU last traded ~$705 (−0.4%) after hours (Nasdaq.com) (Nasdaq.com; The Motley Fool; CNBC, 2026-11-23)

Asia open (23 Nov): Samsung Electronics (−5.4%, ₩173,200) and SK hynix (−5.8%, ₩1.05M) fell in Korean pre-market trading after the 20 Nov US chip rout, in which SK hynix's US ADR fell 13.11% and KOSPI night futures 7.0%; Seoul readied its ₩10.76T market-stabilisation fund, eased buyback order caps for three months from 24 Nov and stepped up illegal short-selling checks (no short-sale ban) (Seoul Economic Daily; Aju Press; Hankyung, 2026-11-23)

Largest HBM customer: Nvidia's board unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang as president, CEO and director with immediate effect, 11 days after he resigned, saying it received input from senior US government officials and is confident his return poses no national-security risk; the independent directors' investigation continues with his cooperation. Nvidia rose 31.48%, regaining nearly $1 trillion in market value; President Trump said Nvidia's internal export-control compliance review should continue (NVIDIA Newsroom; AP, 2026-11-23)

Memory cost pass-through: the FT reports Dell, HPE, Lenovo and Supermicro are seeking AI-server price increases of up to 45% after contracts were signed, mainly because of memory costs; GPU server prices are up at least 20–30% and CPU server nodes have more than tripled. HPE says it now lets orders be repriced if component costs rise and expects high memory and storage prices well into 2027 (TrendForce (citing Financial Times), 2026-11-23)

Competitor targets (Goldman Sachs, third-party est., report dated 22 Nov): Goldman cut Samsung Electronics' target to ₩350,000 from ₩500,000 and SK hynix's to ₩2.0M from ₩3.5M (both still Buy). It sees the shortage persisting through 2027, then CXMT supply and weaker PC/phone demand shrinking the DRAM shortfall from 5.1% in 2027 to 1.2% in 2028, with conventional DRAM prices about −19% to −20% and NAND about −20% in 2028; HBM market $60B (2026) → $200B (2027) → $237B (2028) (Chosun Biz (Goldman Sachs est.); Maeil Business, 2026-11-23)

HBM demand debate (third-party est.): SemiAnalysis reportedly cut its 2028 global HBM bit-demand forecast by ~30% and its 2028 AI-accelerator spending forecast to $758B from $1.054T; KB Securities sees 2027 HBM demand split Nvidia 38%, Google 37%, AMD 13%. SK hynix's largest customer (presumed Nvidia) fell to 14.8% of its 9M 2026 sales from 27% a year earlier; Samsung and SK hynix filings note contract volumes can change with customer demand (Korea JoongAng Daily (KB Securities, SemiAnalysis estimates), 2026-11-22)

Bear view (third-party opinion): Objective Analysis founder Jim Handy told The Korea Times the memory price surge is 'temporary' and that hyperscalers spending ~40% of revenue on capex are likely to slow at some point, which would cause memory prices to collapse, possibly back to 2024 levels; he did not give a timing (The Korea Times, 2026-11-22)

Analyst note (Citi, third-party est.): Atif Malik reiterated Buy and a $1,300 target, calling the memory sell-off overdone; Citi estimates that even if Nvidia-related financing (~14% of hyperscaler capex by its assumption) stopped completely, total DRAM demand would fall only ~12% and NAND ~7%, and expects DRAM and HBM supply to stay constrained through 2027–28, with tighter US equipment curbs limiting bit growth at China fabs (Investing.com; GuruFocus; TipRanks, 2026-11-22)

Largest HBM customer: The New York Times reported on 21 Nov that the SEC's inquiry into Nvidia's accounting is at an early stage and may end without charges; its focus is unconfirmed, and reports note Nvidia's 2025 switch to reporting regional sales by customer headquarters, which removed Singapore from its breakdown. Nvidia and the SEC have not commented; Bloomberg separately reports California's attorney general says his probe also covers potential criminal violations of state law (AFP (via France 24); The New York Times, 2026-11-21)
